title: Enum-typed table field (no EDT) + form exposure + validateWrite downgrade guard on a labelled error
instruction: In the sandbox model, add an ordered service-tier ladder to a custom change-log table and guard it against downgrades. Ground the field rules first with get_knowledge(topic="table fields") and the d365fo_file operation spec for add-field. Build, in this order: (1) an enum DemoServiceTier with exactly four values in ladder order -- None (0), Silver (1), Gold (2), Platinum (3) -- whose own Label is the existing label @SCM:Code; every enum VALUE must also carry an EXISTING label id resolved through the labels index (labels(action="search")), never raw text (BPErrorLabelIsText); do NOT set IsExtensible, extensibility is out of scope for this case. (2) a table DemoTaxChangeLog (Label @TaxTransactionInquiry:HeaderNote, TableGroup=Main) with field ChangeLogId (String, EDT Num, mandatory), a unique alternate-key index ChangeLogIdx on ChangeLogId, a field group Overview containing ChangeLogId, and TitleField1=ChangeLogId. (3) the enum field, in a SINGLE d365fo_file(action=modify, objectType=table, operation="add-field") call: fieldName="ServiceTier", fieldEnumType=<the enum's ACTUAL created name, i.e. the prefixed ConDemoServiceTier>, fieldLabel="@SCM:Description", and NO fieldType. On add-field, fieldType is an EDT NAME, never an XML element name -- passing fieldType="AxTableFieldEnum" fails this case, and so does creating any EDT (an AxEdtEnum wrapper) for this field: an enum table field needs no EDT at all. The written field must be <AxTableField i:type="AxTableFieldEnum"> with <EnumType>ConDemoServiceTier</EnumType> and NO <ExtendedDataType> child; a field that ends up as AxTableFieldString referencing a non-existent EDT is a fail even if it is later repaired. (4) add-field-to-field-group ServiceTier into Overview -- a field in no field group compiles but fails BP (BPErrorTableFieldNotInFieldGroup). The field's label id (@SCM:Description) must stay DIFFERENT from the enum's own label id (@SCM:Code): reusing the enum's label on the field (or on an EDT) is BPErrorFieldLabelIsCopyOfEnumLabel / BPErrorTypeLabelIsCopyOfEnumLabel, which the compiler does not catch. (5) a SimpleListDetails form DemoTaxChangeLogDetails over the table's data source, generated via the form scaffold pattern (formPattern=SimpleListDetails), with the grid showing ChangeLogId; then expose the enum field on it EXCLUSIVELY via d365fo_file(action=modify, operation="add-control") as a ComboBox bound to the data source with DataField=ServiceTier, placed in the details-side group the scaffold produced -- read that group's ACTUAL name back with get_object_info(objectType="form") before writing the control instead of guessing it, and the form must still validate against its form pattern afterwards. (6) set the table's FormRef property to the created form (ConDemoTaxChangeLogDetails), so the metadata chain table -> form is complete. (7) on the table, add the downgrade guard as `public boolean validateWrite()`: assign `boolean ret = super();`, then when `ret && this.RecId != 0 && enum2int(this.ServiceTier) < enum2int(this.orig().ServiceTier)` do `ret = checkFailed("@TaxTransactionInquiry:HeaderNote");`, and `return ret;`. Read the stored value from this.orig() -- do not re-select the record -- and route the message through that EXISTING label: a raw string literal fails the case (BPErrorLabelIsText) and so does creating a new label. Inserts (RecId == 0) and upgrades must pass unchanged. Before concluding that the enum, the field or the label "already exists", verify it: a symbol-index hit is NOT proof -- the index can carry stale rows for objects that are not on disk, so confirm with get_object_info / a file read (and update_symbol_index) first, and never skip a write on the strength of an index row alone. All three objects must build with zero errors and pass a Best Practice run with zero BP errors; the BP evidence must come from a run with an explicit per-object target (a run_bp_check without targetFilter, or with an element type xppbp does not support, reports a false clean) and from a build that actually recompiled these objects (a skipped incremental build is not evidence). Runtime correctness is judged by the SysTest in eval/systests/L3-enum-field-form-downgrade-guard.xml (class EvalL3ServiceTierDowngradeTest), which inserts a Gold row and asserts validateWrite() is false for a Silver downgrade, true for a Platinum upgrade, and true for a fresh insert at any tier.
